title: Multimodal Emotion Recognition
summary: Bachelor's thesis comparing six models across text, audio, and image modalities with three fusion strategies and built-in explainability.
problem: Emotion recognition models trained on a single modality (text, audio, or image alone) miss cues that only surface when the signals are considered together.
approach: Trained and compared six models spanning text, audio, and image inputs; evaluated three fusion strategies for combining them; applied Integrated Gradients and Grad-CAM to explain model predictions; built a feature-caching layer so repeated experiments reused precomputed embeddings instead of recomputing them.
outcome: The feature-caching layer cut experiment turnaround from hours to minutes, making it practical to run far more fusion-strategy comparisons within the thesis timeline.

title: LLM Persona Bias Experiment
summary: A factorial study of how assigning an LLM a persona shifts its outputs, written up as a CATS 2026 submission.
problem: Assigning an LLM a persona (a demographic or professional identity) can bias its outputs, but how much the effect varies across models and prompt types is poorly quantified.
approach: Designed a factorial experiment crossing four LLMs, seven personas, and three prompt types, running five repetitions per cell to control for sampling variance.
outcome: Findings were written up as a submission to CATS 2026, quantifying how persona framing shifts LLM outputs across models and prompt types.

title: TaskFlow
summary: A team productivity and task-management web app built with ASP.NET Core MVC.

title: Library Management Database
summary: A relational database for a library system, built in Oracle PL/SQL: books, authors, publishers, loans, and reservations, with stored procedures for activity reports and triggers that archive loan history.

title: BacPeBune
summary: A two-person Best-Fit memory allocator using mmap for direct memory management, mutexes for thread safety, and memory protection to guard allocated regions, minimizing internal and external fragmentation for multithreaded workloads.
